rationale:
RESUBMISSION on the veto of 2026-08-23 18:07. The guardian's safest contained alternative was: resubmit edit 1 with only the ComponentID-deletion hunk, and file the rendered_template_sha provenance feature as its own plan. Both halves now exist, and this round also owes the council an account of what that hunk actually WAS, because the veto — correct on its own terms — convicted the wrong author.

THE UNDISCLOSED HUNK WAS ANOTHER SESSION'S UNCOMMITTED WORK, NOT A FEATURE OF MINE. My edit-1 sketch was the live git diff of rerender_page_sections_action.go. Between my morning hunk-verification and my 18:56 commit, the 357/RFC_046 lane's provenance call-site landed uncommitted in that shared file; the diff I sketched carried it, and the pathspec commit took it as a same-file passenger. Every signal read safe: the clean-HEAD-extract build PASSED (their struct field was already committed — a green build proves compilability, not authorship), and my hunk check had been true when I ran it. The full account is in WRONG_CALLS 2026-08-24, and the mechanism's owner has been told by CONTRIB into bugfix_357_component_identity, because four seats' HIGH objections about rendered_template_sha are THEIRS to answer and were addressed to a round they never saw.

WHAT THE COUNCIL SHOULD KNOW ABOUT THAT MECHANISM, so the 'nonexistent column' finding does not stand unanswered: rendered_template_sha is not a column write. It is an in-flight out-field which the save step RESOLVES to the dormant page_components.component_version_id column (RFC_046 phase 1, commit bbe178309, owner ruled option 1 on 2026-08-22 — a design that also answers reuse_agent's content_hash/rendered_html_digest question, since it reuses a dormant column rather than adding a third digest). Measured 2026-08-24: component_version_id populated on 32 of 2001 rows, consistent with that lane's phase-0 un-severing landing this morning. Judging that design remains their round's business, not this one's.

EACH REMAINING OBJECTION, ACTED ON RATHER THAN ARGUED:
- guardian edit-3 (unrecorded 247/250 replay): CLOSED. Both files recorded via the runner's own --record-only with the artifact check its documentation demands, done first and stated in the notes column ('effect verified live 2026-08-24: component exists, active, id line converted'). The replay hazard is now shut at the ledger, not merely blunted at the file.
- editquality edit-2 (the '<no value>' vs 'empty string' contradiction): RECONCILED at the code — they are two STAGES of one path, not two mechanisms. missingkey=zero renders an unbound key as '<no value>'; component_library.go:1170-1171 then strips that string to '', which is how id="" reaches a page. Both of my descriptions were right about different stages and wrong to appear unreconciled; the four idea.uk pages serving <section id=""> are this exact two-stage path's live output.
- editquality edit-5 (sketch used placeholder syntax for SQL claimed APPLIED): the COMMITTED file carries the literal statements — the placeholders were my sketch-side abbreviation, a compression that was exactly wrong for a reviewer, and this round's sketches are verbatim git show output.
- guardian edit-5 (after-the-fact submission): acknowledged without defence, and it is the estate's stated design (owner ruling 2026-07-29: on a shared-HEAD tree, review here is after the fact, by design). The WHERE guards make replay idempotent; that is now stated rather than implied.
- bug_historian HIGH (missingkey=zero root behaviour and reElementID's id="" blindness left live): NOT settled by this round, and deliberately so — it is the open architecture decision on RFC_032 (§9c/9d), now in front of the owner with production evidence attached: an unrelated content backfill re-collided 3 of the 12 repaired pages within hours, and the corpus-level counts stayed green throughout. The seat's point that deferring detector fixes has cost content before is quoted in that RFC section rather than paraphrased.

WHAT THIS ROUND ASKS THE COUNCIL TO REVIEW: the retirement AS COMMITTED AND LIVE — the two deleted bindings (my hunks verbatim below), the seed-file id fixes, the ledger recordings — with the passenger disclosed and owned elsewhere. The third binding (v3_site_actions.go:2385) remains live and uncommitted-by-me for the same reason as before, now with a second occupant: the file today carries the 345 lane's uncommitted call-site hunk, and committing it would repeat the exact passenger failure this round exists to account for. It is inert (zero templates spell the placeholder — census re-run 2026-08-24) and named in the lane handoff with the exact edit to make once the file is clean.

commit 024303681771db43f2315055cfc4537f250c8388
Author: cqls <aaa@designconsultancy.co.uk>
Date:   Sun Aug 23 18:56:55 2026 +0100

    RFC_032 step 3: retire the ComponentID bindings - two of three deleted, the third named rather than committed because its file would break HEAD
    
    Owner ruling RFC_032 section 8 is converge on InstanceID and retire
    ComponentID. Step 2 converted the templates this morning; this is the
    retirement.
    
    THE ORDER IS THE WHOLE RISK. The renderer runs missingkey=zero, so a
    placeholder with no binding does not error - it renders EMPTY. A template
    still spelling id="{{.ComponentID}}" after this change renders id="", and the
    collision detector cannot see that: reElementID is \sid="([^"{}]+)" and the +
    requires at least one character. Deleting too early produces an invalid page
    that every automated check calls clean. Not hypothetical: four idea.uk guide
    pages serve <section id=""> today, and I fetched one to confirm it.
    
    So the precondition is zero and it is measured, not assumed. A census over
    EVERY live table with a template-or-html column - a DO block over
    information_schema rather than a guess at which table matters - found the
    placeholder in exactly two places: component_versions (history, which is its
    job) and content_components, which held THREE rows, not the one an
    is_active-filtered query had shown me earlier. pricing was active with no
    placements; header and footer were inactive with none, same 2025-11-21 library
    seed. All three are now converted and the count is 0.
    
    Those three could not go through the pipeline for a structural reason worth
    recording: the conversion files one work item per component, site_work_items
    .site_id is NOT NULL, and a template's site is only reachable through the
    pages that place it. Zero placements means no honest site, so the
    placement-driven seed skips them silently. They were converted by the real
    converter and passed the real gate, each with a control proving the gate
    REFUSES the unconverted original; only the persistence is by hand, mirroring
    writeScopedTemplate and guarded so a re-run is a no-op. The two inactive rows
    were done deliberately - they cannot render today, but after this change a
    reactivated row is exactly the invisible-empty-id case.
    
    The two seed files are part of the same hole. Both create their component with
    the placeholder, both carry ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE, and neither is
    recorded in schema_migrations - so the runner's own pending test treats them
    as pending and a migration run would overwrite two templates converted this
    morning. One line changed in each, the id, so no other replay hazard those
    files carry is widened by me.
    
    WHAT IS NOT HERE. The third binding, v3_site_actions.go:2385, is edited in the
    working tree and deliberately NOT committed. That file carries another
    session's uncommitted work - five further hunks calling three functions in
    section_metadata_keys.go, which is UNTRACKED and absent from HEAD. Committing
    it by pathspec would take their half-finished work with mine and put calls to
    undefined symbols on the shared branch, breaking the build for every session.
    It is inert to leave: with zero templates referencing the placeholder, a
    binding nothing reads changes no output. Named here, in the lane NOTES and in
    RFC_032 so it is finished rather than forgotten.
    
    Full actions suite green, built and tested from a clean git archive HEAD
    extract taken AFTER HEAD moved - the first extract was stale and its failure
    is what surfaced the other session's WIP in the first place.
    
    Council-Submitted: e8c7414c-426d-4aee-a0ca-3e2e2400cbec

plan.risks:
1) THIS ROUND DOES NOT SETTLE THE DETECTOR QUESTION. bug_historian's HIGH — missingkey=zero's silent-empty behaviour and reElementID's id="" blindness stay live for the next author — is the standing architecture decision on RFC_032, in front of the owner with the §9d production evidence. A reviewer who believes it must not be deferred should say so to THAT track; approving this round approves the retirement, not the deferral.

2) THE THIRD BINDING IS STILL LIVE. v3_site_actions.go:2385 binds a key no template reads. Deleting it today means committing a file that currently carries the 345 lane's uncommitted hunk — the exact passenger failure this round accounts for. The deferral is a judgement that an inert binding is cheaper than a repeat; a reviewer may disagree.

3) THE PASSENGER ITSELF IS NOT RE-REVIEWED HERE. Its mechanism (RFC_046) has its own lane, own commits, own owner ruling; the four HIGH objections about it are routed there by CONTRIB. If that lane has no council trail of its own covering the reuse question, those objections stand and are theirs.

4) RECORD-ONLY IS A ONE-WAY DOOR. If either 247/250 recording is ever wrong — the artifact check mistaken — the runner will skip a file that needed applying, for ever. The notes columns carry the exact check performed so a future reader can re-verify rather than trust.
